clean_source_blocks.text: A note left by one of the teenage suspects contains general "hate rhetoric", investigators say.

Authorities in the United States say three people have been killed at a complex housing a mosque and an Islamic school in San Diego in a suspected hate-motivated attack. San Diego Police chief Scott Wahl said the two shooters in the incident at the Islamic Center of San Diego (ICSD) in southern California on Monday were also found dead of apparent self-inflicted gunshot wounds. “Because of the Islamic centre location, we are considering this a hate crime until it’s not,” Wahl told reporters. The suspects were two males, believed to be aged 17 and 19, according to the police chief. Wahl said one of the victims was a security guard at the Islamic centre, who played a “pivotal role” in ensuring that the incident did not become far worse.

Three people have been killed in a shooting at a mosque in San Diego, California, which officials believe was perpetrated by two teenage attackers. The shooting took place on Monday morning as officers were investigating a call about a possibly suicidal teen who had run away from home. At 11:43 local time (19:43 BST), police were called to a shooting at the Islamic Center of San Diego, and found three victims who had been shot in the front of the building. Shortly after, they received another call that shots had been fired nearby at a landscaper from a vehicle. When officers arrived at the second scene, they found the suspects - ages 17 and 18 - dead of self-inflicted wounds.

The woman said he had gone with a companion, and both were dressed in camouflage. A note the youth left behind included "generalised hate rhetoric and hate speech". Wahl said police found the suspect's behaviour to be "not consistent" with someone who is considered suicidal. Investigators then went to a local high school, where one of the teens studied, as well as a shopping mall where the car had been reported seen. Wahl added that the motive for the attack is currently not known, but presumed to be a hate crime due to the location and the prominence of the mosque. He added that the note contained no specific threat to the mosque, or to any other location or individual.

[Lähde: BBC World]
Three people have been killed in a shooting at a mosque in San Diego, California, which officials believe was perpetrated by two teenage attackers.

The shooting took place on Monday morning as officers were investigating a call about a possibly suicidal teen who had run away from home.

At 11:43 local time (19:43 BST), police were called to a shooting at the Islamic Center of San Diego, and found three victims who had been shot in the front of the building.

Shortly after, they received another call that shots had been fired nearby at a landscaper from a vehicle. When officers arrived at the second scene, they found the suspects - ages 17 and 18 - dead of self-inflicted wounds.

Among the deceased victims was a security guard who worked at the centre and heroically prevented more people from dying, officials said without providing further details.

The incident is being investigated as a hate crime, according to the FBI, due to writings found by one of the suspect's mother.

Police were first called to the centre at 11:43 local time (19:43 BST) and "observed what appeared to be three deceased victims out front", San Diego Police Chief Scott Wahl said during a news conference on Monday.

"There were no officers involved in firing their weapons," Wahl said, and there was no sign of any gunman.

Before the attack, the mother of one of the suspects had called officers at 9:42 local time, and reported that when her son left, he took several of her guns and her car.

The woman said he had gone with a companion, and both were dressed in camouflage. A note the youth left behind included "generalised hate rhetoric and hate speech".

Wahl said police found the suspect's behaviour to be "not consistent" with someone who is considered suicidal. Investigators then went to a local high school, where one of the teens studied, as well as a shopping mall where the car had been reported seen.

Wahl added that the motive for the attack is currently not known, but presumed to be a hate crime due to the location and the prominence of the mosque. He added that the note contained no specific threat to the mosque, or to any other location or individual.

San Diego Police Chief Scott Wahl said “hate rhetoric” was involved in the deadly shooting at a San Diego mosque that left five people dead, including the two suspects.

Wahl said the shooting that took place on Monday morning at the Islamic Center of San Diego is being investigated as a hate crime.

Authorities in the United States say three people have been killed at a complex housing a mosque and an Islamic school in San Diego in a suspected hate-motivated attack.

San Diego Police chief Scott Wahl said the two shooters in the incident at the Islamic Center of San Diego (ICSD) in southern California on Monday were also found dead of apparent self-inflicted gunshot wounds.

“Because of the Islamic centre location, we are considering this a hate crime until it’s not,” Wahl told reporters.

The suspects were two males, believed to be aged 17 and 19, according to the police chief.

Wahl said one of the victims was a security guard at the Islamic centre, who played a “pivotal role” in ensuring that the incident did not become far worse.

He added that authorities are investigating and working “figure out and piece together exactly what led to this moment”.

All three victims were adults. Children at the school were not physically harmed, according to authorities.

The San Diego Police Department had reported an active shooter incident at the ICSD before saying that the threat was “neutralised”.

Taha Hassane, the imam of the mosque, described the ICSD as a place for people — including non-Muslims — to come together and pray, learn and celebrate.

“It is extremely outrageous to target a place of worship. Our Islamic Center is a place of worship,” Hassane said.

San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria stressed that “hate has no place” in the city.

payload.title: Kolme kuoli ampumisessa San Diegon islamilaiskeskuksessa
payload.summary: Viranomaiset tutkivat San Diegossa tapahtunutta ampumista epäiltynä viharikoksena. Kolme ihmistä kuoli Islamic Center of San Diegon edustalla, ja kaksi nuorta epäiltyä löydettiin myöhemmin kuolleina ilmeisesti itse aiheutettuihin ampumavammoihin.
payload.content:
Kolme ihmistä on kuollut ampumisessa San Diegossa sijaitsevassa islamilaiskeskuksessa, jossa toimii moskeija ja islamilainen koulu. Poliisi tutkii tapausta epäiltynä viharikoksena tapahtumapaikan ja keskuksen näkyvän aseman vuoksi, mutta viranomaisten mukaan hyökkäyksen tarkka motiivi ei ole vielä selvillä.

## Poliisi löysi uhrit keskuksen edustalta

San Diegon poliisipäällikkö Scott Wahlin mukaan poliisi sai maanantaina kello 11.43 paikallista aikaa ilmoituksen ampumisesta Islamic Center of San Diegossa Etelä-Kaliforniassa. Paikalta löydettiin kolme ihmistä, joita oli ammuttu rakennuksen etuosassa.

Yksi kuolleista oli islamilaiskeskuksen vartija. Wahlin mukaan vartijalla oli keskeinen rooli siinä, ettei tilanne muuttunut vielä pahemmaksi. Viranomaiset eivät lähdetietojen perusteella ole kertoneet uhrien nimiä.

Poliisi oli jo ennen ampumisilmoitusta selvittämässä tapausta, jossa kotoaan lähteneen nuoren epäiltiin mahdollisesti olevan itsetuhoinen. Poliisin mukaan nuori oli lähtenyt liikkeelle toisen henkilön kanssa, ja molempien kerrottiin pukeutuneen maastokuvioisiin vaatteisiin.

## Epäillyt löydettiin kuolleina toiselta tapahtumapaikalta

Pian moskeijalla tapahtuneen ampumisen jälkeen poliisi sai toisen ilmoituksen laukauksista lähellä sijaitsevalla alueella. Ilmoituksen mukaan ajoneuvosta oli ammuttu maisematyöntekijää kohti. Kun poliisit saapuivat toiselle paikalle, he löysivät kaksi nuorta miesepäiltyä kuolleina. Viranomaisten mukaan he näyttävät kuolleen itse aiheutettuihin ampumavammoihin.

Lähteissä epäiltyjen iästä on hieman vaihtelevia tietoja, mutta poliisin mukaan kyse oli kahdesta nuoresta miehestä. Ainakin toisen kerrottiin opiskelleen paikallisessa lukiossa. Tutkijat tarkistivat myös koulun sekä ostoskeskuksen, jossa epäiltyjen auton oli kerrottu aiemmin nähdyn.

## Viesti sisälsi yleistä vihapuhetta

Wahlin mukaan yhden epäillyn jättämässä viestissä oli yleistä viharetoriikkaa ja vihapuhetta. Poliisin mukaan viestissä ei kuitenkaan ollut yksilöityä uhkausta moskeijaa, muuta paikkaa tai tiettyä henkilöä vastaan.

Poliisipäällikkö sanoi, että epäillyn toiminta ei vastannut sitä, mitä poliisi pitäisi tyypillisenä itsetuhoisena käyttäytymisenä. Hänen mukaansa tapausta pidetään viharikoksena, kunnes tutkinta osoittaa toisin, koska isku kohdistui islamilaiskeskukseen. Samalla viranomaiset korostavat, ettei motiivista ole vielä lopullista varmuutta.

payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu paketissa olleisiin BBC:n ja Al Jazeeran tietoihin. Epäiltyjen tarkkoja ikiä ei yksilöity, koska lähteissä oli ristiriita 17/18 ja 17/19 välillä.

Shortly after, they received another call that shots had been fired nearby at a landscaper from a vehicle. When officers arrived at the second scene, they found the suspects - ages 17 and 18 - dead of self-inflicted wounds.

The woman said he had gone with a companion, and both were dressed in camouflage. A note the youth left behind included "generalised hate rhetoric and hate speech". Wahl said police found the suspect's behaviour to be "not consistent" with someone who is considered suicidal. Investigators then went to a local high school, where one of the teens studied, as well as a shopping mall where the car had been reported seen. Wahl added that the motive for the attack is currently not known, but presumed to be a hate crime due to the location and the prominence of the mosque. He added that the note contained no specific threat to the mosque, or to any other location or individual.
